comparisons.name: quicktime-light
comparisons.description: QuickTime Player's floating controller laid out as in the Aqua capture (880 x 150 px at 1143, 1325 of Light-QuickTime), over one flat grey, #707070. No comparison with the capture is made: the panel is a vibrant material and its glyphs add light to it, so in the capture every pixel of it is partly a third party's movie, which the library does not reproduce, and with the movie masked nothing is left to score. Over a flat grey the panel's colours follow from the tokens, and these pixels hold them: the panel's size, its 4 pt corners, its edges without a border, seven glyphs, the volume knob and the timeline at the places measured in the capture. The time codes are text in the fallback font and the Share glyph is a thin outline: neither is checked.

comparisons.name: quicktime-light-knob
comparisons.description: The one part of the controller that is opaque, compared with the Aqua capture: the volume knob at the slider's maximum, 11 by 11 pt at 71, 19 pt of the panel, with a 2 pt border of its box masked (the corners outside the circle and its edge, which lie over the movie). Nothing else of the controller is compared with the capture: everything else in it is the panel's material or a glyph that adds light to it, over a third party's movie which the library does not reproduce (see quicktime-light). The score covers the colour of the knob's opaque interior only: the crop is the knob's own box, so the knob's place in the controller is held by the expected pixels of quicktime-light, not here.

comparisons.name: material-two-tone-light
comparisons.description: The controller's translucency over a backdrop of two flat abstract tones that meet under the middle of the panel: slate blue #5a6e82 left of 220 pt, sand #a08c6e right of it. No screenshot is compared: the tones are taken from no picture. Every expected colour is computed from the tokens: the backdrop blurred by 30 pt (a Gaussian whose standard deviation is 30 pt, mirrored at the panel's edges), saturated to 180% (--mac-material-filter, provisional), under --mac-hud-window-controller-material, #1e1e1e at 20% (provisional); a glyph adds white at 48% (--mac-hud-window-vibrant, measured strength). The pixels show that the panel lets its backdrop through, saturates it, tints it and blurs it by about the token's radius, and that a glyph adds light to a coloured fill. They do not show that these values are Catalina's: over a real picture the recipe is still unverified.
